newsitem.title: USA: Heinz reviewing assets, eyes restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Heinz reviewing assets, eyes restructuring.

text.p: Heinz Co Chairman and Chief Executive Anthony O'Reilly said Tuesday the company was reviewing all its assets and considering restructuring its portfolio to ensure maximum capital profits for shareholders.

"We will divest ourselves of assets which do not play to the major strengths I have outlined to you -- the famous six-point plan," O'Reilly told the company's annual shareholder meeting, referring to the six core categories of foodservice, infant foods, ketchup and condiments, pet food, tuna and weight control.

"If we are successful with this plan -- and we are satisfied we will be -- we will use the surplus generated to reduce debt, write off underperforming assets and pay for organizational changes, if these prove necessary," he said.
"We will not rely upon these profits to achieve our goal of double-digit growth over the next few years," he added.
O'Reilly said the company's six core categories had "plenty of room for expansion".

Heinz President and Chief Operating Officer William Johnson told the meeting the company expected sales in the infant foods category to grow to $1.4 billion in three years as a result of rising living standards throughout the world and high birth rates in developing countries.
Johnson also said unit sales in the tuna category was expected to grow 25 percent in two years.
